value.body: A CFD (computational fluid dynamics) engineer uses software to simulate how air, gas or liquid flows around or through a product — a wing, an engine part, a car body or a cooling system. Employers include aerospace and automotive companies, engineering services firms, simulation software vendors and research labs. Most of the day goes into setting up models, running simulations on workstations or clusters, and checking and reporting results.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Aerospace or Mechanical; many roles prefer an M.Tech

items.label: GATE Aerospace Engineering (AE) paper
items.source: GATE 2025 Statistical and Performance Report, IIT Roorkee

items.label: Postgraduate students in aeronautical engineering
items.note: M.Tech/M.E.-level enrolment; ~500 more at Ph.D. level
items.source: AISHE (Ministry of Education) 2023-24, Table 13 (based on actual responses)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join engineering services or simulation firms as trainee analysts, often after a project or internship in CFD. Research and specialist roles commonly ask for an M.Tech or MS in fluid or thermal engineering.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Judging whether results make physical sense

value.title: At a glance
items: The work is desk- and computer-based rather than on the shop floor.
Higher study is common for this role.
Next roles: senior analyst, aerodynamics lead, simulation methods engineer.
